partitor 0.11.0

From score to parts

How to turn a score PDF into large-print parts for your ensemble. You work in a terminal: on Linux (supported), over SSH from a phone or PC or on the same machine; on Windows, in PowerShell; on macOS, in Terminal (best effort). partitor keeps everything in the library folder (local, or on a NAS). Only the build takes long, so make every change first, review it, and build once.

  1. 1DropPDF into the inbox
  2. 2Analyseproof of who plays what, 1–5 min
  3. 3Editnames, choices, groups, layout
  4. 4Reviewone screen, every setting
  5. 5Buildthe part PDFs, minutes

Dashed: the steps that take time. You can go back from Review to Edit as often as you like; nothing is printed until you build.

Before you start

What you need

On every system you need:

  • A library folder with two folders inside, inbox and library. You copy score PDFs into inbox; partitor makes everything else in library. See STORAGE-LOCAL.md or STORAGE-SMB.md for Linux.
  • A score PDF: a vector PDF (from notation software) or a scan. Scans at 300 dpi greyscale work best.

What else you need depends on the system:

  • Linux (Ubuntu LTS), supported. A terminal on the partitor host, or an SSH app on your phone or PC, logged in as a user that can use sudo. Start partitor with sudo partitor (partitor if you are root).
  • Windows, best effort (experimental). The setup program from the Download page, and PowerShell. Start partitor with partitor.
  • macOS, best effort (not supported). Python, Tesseract and a copy of the source (steps below), and Terminal. Start partitor with venv/bin/python lib/partitor-engine in the source folder.

Everything after this section is the same on all systems. Where the guide says “run partitor”, use the start command of your system.

Linux

Follow INSTALL.md once (four commands). The library is /var/lib/partitor/library. Copy a PDF in with cp score.pdf /var/lib/partitor/library/inbox/, or with SFTP or your file manager. The engine runs in a sandbox and never as root.

Windows (PowerShell)

Run partitor-<version>-setup.exe from the Download page. It needs no administrator rights, adds partitor to your PATH and asks for the library folder (default Documents\partitor). Open a new PowerShell window, then:

partitor

The Start menu entry “partitor” opens the same menu. Copy PDFs into Documents\partitor\inbox with File Explorer or Copy-Item score.pdf $HOME\Documents\partitor\inbox\. Paths in this guide use /; on Windows type \.

Limits: one worker (builds are slower), no sandbox (open only PDFs you trust), and the installer is not signed. All limits: platforms/windows/README.md.

macOS (Terminal)

There is no installer and no sandbox yet. The tests run on macOS in CI as a best-effort job; nobody supports this. Open only PDFs you trust. With Homebrew and a clone of the repository, run in Terminal (ADDRESS is the address in step 2 of INSTALL.md):

brew install python@3.12 tesseract
git clone ADDRESS ~/partitor
cd ~/partitor
python3.12 -m venv venv
venv/bin/pip install --only-binary=:all: -r requirements.txt
mkdir -p ~/partitor-library/inbox ~/partitor-library/library
export PARTITOR_LIBRARY=~/partitor-library
venv/bin/python lib/partitor-engine

Check out the newest release tag first if you want a fixed version (git checkout --detach TAG). In a new Terminal window, run export PARTITOR_LIBRARY=~/partitor-library again, or put the line in ~/.zshrc. Copy PDFs into ~/partitor-library/inbox with Finder or cp.

One command. Type partitor and press Enter. Everything else is a menu: you answer with a number or a letter. Enter accepts the value shown in [brackets]; q stops and keeps what is done.

Stage 1

Drop the PDF in the inbox

  1. Copy the score PDF into the inbox folder of the library.
  2. Run partitor (the start command of your system is in the first section). The menu shows the pieces newest first, each under its own fixed number (the serial of its id: 12 is 2026-10-0012, the same number the commands take) and n new from inbox (1 waiting). With many pieces, the five changed last come first as A–E; * marks a piece with work pending. /Bach shows only matching pieces (composer, title, part), / shows all again, + and - turn the page.
  3. Press n, then the number of the PDF, then the pages of the piece (Enter for all pages, or a range such as 8-9 when the PDF holds several pieces).

The PDF moves out of the inbox into a new folder in the library, named by its id, for example 2026-10-0001 (year, month, number).

Stage 2 · takes 1–5 minutes

Analyse and check the proof

partitor reads every page: staves, systems, barlines, bar numbers, staff labels. It does not make any parts yet.

The proof

When it finishes, open the proof in the item folder:

library/2026-10-0001-bach-example-piece/2026-10-0001-proof.pdf

On Windows the path has \\ instead of /.

  • Each page of the proof is a page of the score.
  • Each system has its name in blue, for example p8.s2 (page 8, system 2).
  • Each staff shows the part it goes to. Follow one part down the pages to check that it continues without jumps.

Red frame. A system in a red frame is one partitor is not sure of. Its staves show ? name, the suggestion. You answer these in stage 3.

If the analysis itself is wrong (wrong pages, a staff missed), you can run it again later with y in the item menu, or partitor analyse ID. partitor analyse --all runs it for every item, and asks nothing (open choices stay for the build). A failed analysis also leaves a proof, with the problem marked in red.

Stage 3

Edit: names, choices, groups, layout

The wizard asks these in order. Every answer is saved at once but nothing is built, so you can stop with q and come back later.

Title and composer

Title, then the composer's full name (printed on page 1), then a short form for the head of the inside pages (suggested: the surname). Change them later with m.

Part names

The names come from the printed staff labels. Change one at a time, then Enter when done:

Type Does
7=Organ renames part 7
7=- no PDF for part 7; it stays in the list, marked “not extracted”
7=+ makes the PDF for part 7 again
7+8 joins part 7 into part 8: one part on two staves (a keyboard)
7=-; 8=Continuo several in one line: basso continuo only, from a keyboard part

Choices for the red systems

For each uncertain system the wizard shows where it is (source page, system from the top, proof page), its clefs and labels, and the suggestion as part numbers. Answer with one part number per staff, top staff first:

[1/9] p8.s2: source page 8, system 2 of 4 from the top (proof page 8) 3 staves, clefs top to bottom: F4 G2 F4 suggestion: Bass Trombone, Continuo, Continuo (= 6 7 7) part number for each of the 3 staves, top first (Enter = suggestion; 0 = leave out; same number twice = one part on two staves; j = join with the system below): 6 7 7
  • Enter takes the suggestion.
  • A corrected answer becomes the suggestion for the next systems with the same clefs: press Enter there.
  • 0 leaves a staff out (a staff you left out shows as “(left out)” and 0 in the suggestion); the same number twice puts one part on two staves.
  • j says that this system and the one below it on the page are one system (the analysis took them apart: a system of 4 staves above one of 13 on a page that has 17). The analysis runs again and the questions start over; the join is kept by every later analysis. From the command line: partitor analyse ID --join p5:4 (no system ends after staff 4 of source page 5; --unjoin p5:4 takes it back).
  • d (or 0 for every staff) leaves the whole system out: a title, or the end of another piece above the music. A dropped system counts no bars, the proof marks it “dropped”, and every later analysis keeps it. From the command line: partitor analyse ID --drop p1.s1 (no analysis is run); --undrop p1.s1 puts it back and the choices ask for its parts.
  • A scan that begins with the end of another piece: when a title stands low on the first page, above a system, and systems lie above it, the choices first ask whether those systems are to be dropped (default: no). Look at the proof or at the score before you answer. partitor analyse ID --yes asks nothing and prints the --drop command instead.
  • q stops the questions; continue later with r in the item menu.
  • The proof is drawn again after each answer.

Bar numbers

When a piece starts with a short bar, the wizard asks: p a pickup (Enter), i an incipit (the original notation of the opening: it stays in the part, has no number, and the next bar is 1) or n neither. When a repeat splits a bar, it asks Y/n. Check a few numbers against the proof. Correct later with n: p 1 pickup on or off, i 1 incipit on or off, s 22 1 bar 1 of line 22 completes the bar before it (a half bar over a line break; both halves keep one number), f 3=16 line 3 starts at bar 16, j 4 1 join a false barline, b 4 list the bars of line 4. The proof shows the barline ticks, the bar numbers (magenta) and the rehearsal letters (boxed): press v, open the proof, and press Enter to save. partitor proof 12 draws it again from the saved file.

Groups (optional)

A group prints several parts together as a small score, for example the four trombones. Press n at “Build now?”, then g in the item menu, and type Trombones=2,4,5,6 (part numbers). Trombones= deletes the group. The group becomes one more PDF; staves of other parts leave no gap, and each staff is labelled.

Cue lines (optional)

A singer or player with a long rest can see where another voice enters: a small staff of that voice above the rest, or a word such as "Canto". Nothing is added unless you ask. Press u in the item menu (u Trombones for one part or group), pick the part that gets the cue, and read the table of its long rests. Then type a line:

  • 3=97-98: the music of part 3 (a number of the parts list, or its name) in bars 97 to 98. The cue is the same bars of the source. One bar: 3=97.
  • "Canto"=97: only the word, at bar 97.
  • Options after the bars: noclef (no clef at the start), nolabel (no name above), label=Text, size=0.5 (from 0.3 to 1; 0.6 is the default, and 1, full size, when fit or sync is set), anchor=25, fit and sync=3 (see below).
  • x 2 takes cue 2 away. Enter ends.

The cue stands above the staff (above the top staff of a group). The bars under it become one multi-bar rest of their own, as wide as the cue, so that the barlines of the cue and of the part meet; the rest before and after it stays as it was.

A cue may run on over a bar where the part plays: Canto=24-25 when the part enters in bar 25. Where the part starts to play (or at the bar you name with anchor=25) the barline of the cue meets the barline of the part, at the size of the cue; the bars of the part after it are not changed, and the last barline of the cue stands where it falls. The bars before the anchor must be rests. Add fit to stretch the cue bars after the anchor sideways to the bars of the part: the barlines then meet. A fitted cue is drawn at full size unless you type size=, so that the stretch is small and the notes keep their shape (at 0.6 the stretch is about 1.7 times and the shapes look squashed; size=0.8 is a compromise). It is a musical choice: use it per cue. sync=3 (it implies fit) goes further: the 3rd note with a stem of the cue bar, counted from its left barline, is put over the first note of the part in that bar (the top staff of a group), so that the entrance lines up; the bar is stretched in two pieces, before and after that note. Rests and whole notes are not counted; two stems that stand together are one note. If the note is not found the build says so and fits the bar without it. Build the part (r) and look at it: partitor warns when it cannot confirm that the part rests in a bar, or when the cue stands above ink. The set before is kept until the next good build. The same line for several parts: partitor cue ID 3=97-98 --parts Tenore,5.

The item menu

Open it any time: partitor, then the item's number. The status line lists what has changed since the last build.

Key Edit (saved, not built)
m title, subtitle, composer (full and short; partitor meta ID from the command line); after a change it offers to rename the folder to match (partitor rename ID does the same)
t part names, not extracted, joined
g groups
n bar numbers and rehearsal marks (m 95: mark at bar 95 on/off; m 95 110 120: several; m 22:1: bar 1 of line 22; letters follow in bar order). ? shows the help with an example; v draws the proof with the edits
e / c expand / contract: one step larger or smaller (pages, then space between staves); asks for a part, Enter = all parts
p number of pages (auto or 1–99)
a paper: Letter → A4 → Ledger (17×11 landscape) → Letter
k ambitus: pick a part, type its range (F3-A4), auto, off or on; Enter keeps it
h short names: the short form of each staff label in a group score. Pick a part, type its short form or auto (the rule); Enter keeps it
u cue lines: a small staff of another voice, or a word, above a rest (u Trombones; see Cue lines above)
s any setting as key=value, e.g. gap=11, reflow=on, large=off
Key Other
v review (stage 4)
y analyse again (new proof; names, groups and settings kept; choices and bar numbers asked again, the previous answers offered)
f fit: which paper and staff size give the best page turns for a part (f Trombones; f Trombones 4 picks option 4, then r). Read-only until you pick. partitor plan ID --group AltTen=Alto,Tenor tries a group the piece does not have. Guide: PLAN-AND-FOLDOUTS.md
l pages: one line for each page of a built part with the turn after it (l Trombones). Move a system to the next page: partitor pages ID Trombones --move 26=1; add --dry-run to see the pages and save nothing; partitor pages ID Trombones --clear drops the manual page breaks and pins of that part. Guide: PLAN-AND-FOLDOUTS.md
x repage: new page breaks from the lines of the last build, no new analysis (x Trombones). A page turn falls only beside a multi-bar rest; a turn while playing is a warning with page and bar. Break a page by hand: s, Trombones:breaks=45,60, then x Trombones. Needs one build with this version or later
r build (stage 5). r Trombones or r 2-4 builds only those parts or groups (numbers as in the file names); the other part files stay
b back to the list
Stage 4

Review everything

Press v in the item menu (or partitor show ID). The wizard also shows this screen before it asks “Build now?”.

The review screen

2026-10-0001 · Example piece · 7 parts · ready to build status: ready to build title: Example piece composer: J. S. Bach short: Bach (from the composer) parts: 1 Canto (G2) — ambitus E4-G5 2 Alto Trombone (C3) — ambitus F3-A4 4 Tenor Trombone I (C4) — ambitus C3-F4 (by hand) 7 Continuo (G2+F4) — two staves, ambitus none (off) group: Trombones: Alto Trombone, Tenor Trombone I, … bars: line starts 1, 3, 6, 9 …; letters A (p10.s3) settings: paper=letter

Check the parts list, the groups and the title. If something is wrong, go back to stage 3; nothing has been built yet.

Ambitus. Each part's lowest and highest note, printed in place of the part name at the start of the first line (in a group score, one per staff), as two stacked black noteheads at 80 % size, as in engravings. Every note counts, so check it: the proof rings each part's lowest and highest note in green, with its bar, page and system; show and k give the bars too, and a doubtful value is marked ? and asked at the end of the analysis, with a suggested range without the doubtful note (Enter takes it, k keeps the value as read). A wrong value is fixed with k (or s and Alto Trombone:ambitus=F3-A4); =auto reads it again from the notes, =off prints none. A part whose clef is a treble clef with an 8 below (tenor voice, alto trombone in some editions) shows the ambitus in that clef, and the text and a hand-set range are the sounding pitch, an octave below the written notes (the staff Alto Trombone written B4-G5 reads B3-G4). Continuo parts have none unless =on.

Status Means Next
not analysed the analysis did not finish y or r
needs choices red systems still open r asks them first
ready to build all set, never built r
changes not built edits since the last build v, then r
built the PDFs match the settings print
Stage 5 · takes minutes

Build and print

Press r. partitor reads the pages again and writes one PDF per part, one per group, and a large-print copy of each. A long score takes several minutes (the pages are read by several workers at once); other services on the host keep running (the build runs at low priority).

From the command line: partitor rebuild ID is the same as r (partitor rebuild ID Trombones builds only that part). partitor set ID key=value --build changes a setting and builds at once; without --build the change is saved, not built. partitor plan ID Trombones is the same as f. Every command and option is in COMMANDS.md.

To change one part (a new gap, a corrected ambitus), edit it, then press r followed by its name or number, for example r Trombones or r 2 4. Only those parts are written again; the other files in parts are not touched. If a name in the list would change (title, composer, part number), partitor builds all parts and says why.

The part files

The parts are in the item's parts folder. The name starts with the part so a player finds it first:

06-bass-trombone-Bach-Example--2026-10-0001.pdf
06-bass-trombone-Bach-Example--2026-10-0001-11x17.pdf
08-trombones-Bach-Example--2026-10-0001.pdf
  • Normal copy: Letter (or A4), printed double-sided. Page turns fall at movement starts, new sections or rests; a section that fits on two pages stands on a facing pair.
  • Large-print copy (-11x17): print on 11×17 (ledger) paper at 100 %, then cut at the dotted line (set cutline=marks for short crop marks, off for none). A4 scores give an -A3 copy instead, no cutting. Paper ledger gives no large copy: the sheet is 11×17 already.
  • Ledger (paper=ledger, menu a): 17×11 in, landscape, for a larger staff (up to 8 mm; Letter holds 3.6–3.8 mm on long lines). The lines are 2.2 times as wide, so there are about twice as many pages. Print double-sided, flip on the short edge (the 11 in side, like a book). Stands for two pages side by side are wide: check the stand first. To fit more systems on a page, set Trombones:group_gap=5 (staff spaces between the staves of a group; also a part on two staves) or gap=7 (space between lines).

Small print. When the score's lines are long, the staff can come out small. partitor then offers re-flow (experimental, off by default; paper=ledger is the alternative): lines cut at barlines with the clef copied, for a staff up to 8 mm, on more pages. It shows the size and pages before and after; you keep it or not. A group (for example the trombones) is cut only at barlines that all its staves have, and stays within 1.5 times its pages unless you set pages. The build prints a re-flow: line: how many lines can be cut and why the others stay whole.

When something goes wrong

Common problems

You seeDo
“library folder not found”The folder does not exist. The NAS or the disk is off or not connected, or the path is wrong. Check it, wait a minute, run partitor again. See STORAGE-SMB.md.
“library folder not readable”The folder exists, but your user may not enter it (folder mode or group). Give your user read access (see INSTALL.md: the group partitor), log in again after a change of group, run partitor again.
“library folder not set up”The folder exists but has no inbox and library inside. Run the set-up again (see INSTALL.md), or point partitor at the right folder.
The wizard stopped (q, lost connection)The item is kept. Open it from the menu and continue; r asks what is still open.
A part is missing on some linesCheck the red systems on the proof; correct with t or analyse again with y.
A page shows two systems (for example 4 and 13 staves) where the score has oneAnswer j in the choices, or partitor analyse ID --join p5:4. The bar numbers of that page are then counted once.
Bar numbers are off from some line onn, then f N=B for the first wrong line.
A part rests for whole systemsNormal: those bars become one rest line with the count (for example 14), so the numbers continue.
